summary: The study describes the direct fabrication of ultrathin, controllable thickness ReS2 films on SiO2/Si substrates using wide-temperature-range (WTR) atomic layer deposition (ALD). The process involves in-situ annealing with H2S to reduce S defects and improve film quality. The ALD process uses ReCl5 and H2S as precursors, with a temperature range of 20–1000 °C. The study highlights the ability to achieve precise thickness control and improved crystallinity through the optimization of ALD cycles and annealing conditions.
evidence: The building of high-quality and especially thickness-controllable ReS2 is the crux of researching it and developing its wider application. In this work, ultrathin (1–5 layers) ReS2 with controllable thickness and improved quality is obtained on SiO2/Si substrates, using wide-temperature-range (WTR) atomic layer deposition (ALD).
